videos.title: The ENTIRE History of the Vatican in 50 minutes
videos.description:
How did a tiny piece of land in the middle of Rome become the smallest country in the world and one of the most influential institutions in human history? This documentary explores the entire history of the Vatican, from the ancient Vatican Hill and the story of Saint Peter to the creation of Vatican City in 1929. Discover how Emperor Constantine built the first St. Peter’s Basilica, how the popes gained political power, and how the Papal States shaped European history. Explore the Donation of Constantine, the mysterious Cadaver Synod, the Great Western Schism, the Renaissance popes, the Borgia family, and the rise of the Swiss Guard. Learn how Michelangelo, Raphael, and other legendary artists transformed the Vatican into one of the greatest centres of art and architecture in the world.

But the Vatican’s history is also filled with conflict, scandals, and dramatic changes. Discover how Martin Luther’s Protestant Reformation challenged the Church, how Napoleon and Italian unification stripped the popes of their territories, and how Mussolini’s Lateran Treaty created the independent State of Vatican City in 1929. This video also explores the Vatican during World War II, the Second Vatican Council, Pope John Paul II, financial scandals, Vatileaks, the Catholic Church abuse crisis, and Pope Benedict XVI’s historic resignation. Finally, take a look inside the world’s smallest country, its secret archives, Vatican Museums, Swiss Guard, and unique traditions. From ancient Rome to the modern papacy, discover the complete story of the Vatican.

videos.title: The Entire History of Karnataka | Part 2
videos.description:
A city the Portuguese called as large as Rome. An emperor who wrote poetry by night and won wars by day. A bazaar of rubies and diamonds, a nine-day festival on a stone platform that still stands, and a single winter's day in 1565 that changed everything.
 
This is Part 2 of the entire history of Karnataka: the rise of Vijayanagara, the golden age of Krishnadevaraya, the Battle of Talikota (Rakkasa-Tangadi), and the Deccan Sultanates who built Bidar and Bijapur.

📜 IN THIS EPISODE
• Harihara and Bukka, Vidyaranya, and the founding of Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra
• Hampi through the eyes of Domingo Paes, Niccolò de' Conti and Abdur Razzaq
• Saluva Timmarusu and the rise of Krishnadevaraya (and which stories are legend)
• The four campaigns – the Bahmani raid, Ummattur, the Portuguese at Goa, the Gajapati war – and the Battle of Raichur (1520)
• The Mahanavami festival and the Mahanavami Dibba, still standing in Hampi
• Amuktamalyada, the Ashtadiggajas, Vyasatirtha, Purandara Dasa and Kanakadasa
• Tenali Ramakrishna – a real poet, and the folklore that grew around him
• Aliya Rama Raya, the alliance of the four sultans and the Battle of Talikota, 23 January 1565
• The Bahmani Sultanate at Gulbarga and Bidar, Bande Nawaz, and Mahmud Gawan's madrasa (1472)
• Ibrahim Adil Shah II and the Kitab-i-Nauras, the Ibrahim Rauza, and the Gol Gumbaz
 
🎬 PART 3 is coming: Kempe Gowda and Bengaluru, the Wodeyars and the Mysore Dasara, Onake Obavva, Rani Abbakka, Kittur Chennamma, the rockets of Mysore, Visvesvaraya, and one Karnataka.
 
If you enjoyed this, subscribe so you don't miss Part 3, and tell us in the comments: which part of Vijayanagara's story should get its own video?
 
📚 NOTES
This episode draws on contemporary accounts and standard histories, including the chronicles of Domingo Paes and Fernão Nuniz (tr. Robert Sewell, A Forgotten Empire, 1900), Cesare Federici's account of Vijayanagara after 1565, UNESCO's description of the Group of Monuments at Hampi, and modern scholarship on the Deccan (including Richard M. Eaton). Figures such as army sizes come from period chroniclers and are flagged on screen as their claims. Traditional stories – like Timmarusu's tale and the Tenali Ramakrishna anecdotes – are labelled as legend or folklore. Disputed points, such as the claim that commanders switched sides at Talikota, are presented as disputed.

videos.title: A Radio Signal with an Unexpected Listener
videos.description:
In 1980s Brazil, Clip Informática on Radio USP in São Paulo sent computer programs over the air as sound. A listener could record the signal onto cassette; a compatible home computer could then try to read its patterns as data. The path ran from station to radio, cassette, and computer—but distortion, recording level, playback speed, and compatibility all mattered.

Datassette catalogues its copy of episode 102 with a 1987 date and MSX software audio near the end. Separately, developer Weber Kai identified an online recording as episode 102 and described trying to decode it.

Kai reported a match with the MSX game Avenger. We haven’t independently repeated his decoding, established that the two recordings are identical, or verified a game launch. His public notes do not provide a complete comparison record.
